rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root شقق centers on division or separation and extends to sides, halves, parties, distance, hardship, splitting speech or wood, and related forms.
rows.anchor: الجانب لأنه مفارق للجانب الآخر ، واسم لما نظرت إليه لأنه في جانب واحد ، وجنس من أجناس الجن لأنه فرقة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although others explain شقائق النعمان by red color resembling lightning, he derives the name from the flower's split, layered petals gathered together.
rows.anchor: كذا قالوا ، وعندي أنها سميت لتفرق أوراقها وتصفقها فكأنها مشققة مع التجمع

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports that the last revealed verse concerned kalala inheritance and that the last revealed sura was Bara'a; al-Biqai cites al-Bukhari.
rows.anchor: عن البراء رضي الله عنه قال : آخر آية نزلت { يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة } وآخر سورة نزلت براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bara'a's opening repudiation of those feared to break treaties explains the close of al-Anfal, so al-Anfal precedes this longer sura despite its obscurity and length.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت مناسبة أولها - الداعي إلى البراءة مم ن يخشى نقضه - لآخر الأنفال المبين لمن يصلح للولاية

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Uthman says the Prophet directed placement of revealed material but died without clarifying whether Bara'a belonged to al-Anfal; their similar subject led Uthman to join them without a basmala.
rows.anchor: فقال عثمان رضي الله عنه : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مما - وقال الستي : ربما - يأتي عليه الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uthman placed the pair among the long suras because they resembled one another, whether or not they constituted one sura.
rows.anchor: فبين أنهما اشتبها عليه وأنه وضعهما في الطول

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon counts the seventh of the seven long suras as Yunus, or as al-Anfal and Bara'a together if they are one sura.
rows.anchor: والسابعة سورة يونس أو الأنفال وبراءة جميعا لأنهما سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says al-Anfal and al-Tawba may be one sura: both concern fighting and total 206 verses, making them the seventh long sura.
rows.anchor: سورة الأنفال والتوية سورة واحدة كلتاهما نزلت في القتال تعدان اتلسابعة من الطول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold that the two are separate suras; a gap accommodates that view, while omitting the basmala accommodates the view that they are one.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هما سورتان فتركت بينهما فرجة لقول من يقول : هما سورتان ، وتركت ' بسم ' لقول من يقول : هما سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy explains their placement together by saying al-Anfal mentions covenants while Bara'a repudiates covenants.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي كعب رضي الله عنه أنه قال : إنما توهموا ذلك لأن في الأنفال ذكر العهود ، وفي براءة نبذ العهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers defining mathani in relation to the mufassal: the mufassal is the first collective label by sura length, followed by mathani, mi'un, then the long suras.
rows.anchor: والأحسن كون ذلك بالنسبة إلى اغلمفصل من وجهين : الأول أن المفصل أول لقب جامع للسور باعتبار القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason for calling them mathani is that reciting portions of them across the two prayer cycles resembles reciting two short suras from the mufassal.
rows.anchor: أنها لما زادت على المفصل كانت قسمة السورة منها في ركعتين من الصلاة كقراءة سورتين من المفصل

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq transmits through unnamed companions that Muhammad ibn Yazid said the sura's opening basmala was not written.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق : جدثني بعض أصحابنا عن صاحبنا محمد بن يزيد

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas asked Ali why the basmala was omitted here; Ali answered that the basmala is a guarantee of safety.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : سألت عليا رضي الله عنه : لم تكتب ' بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ' ها هنا ؟ قال : لأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ' أمان

rows.speaker: الشاطبي
rows.claim: Al-Shatibi's poem says that whether one joins to or begins with Bara'a, its sword-revelation is recited without the basmala.
rows.anchor: ومهما تصلها أو بدأت براءة … تنزيلها بالسيف لست مبسملا

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the basmala signifies peace and safety, so it is not written in repudiation and warfare; letters inviting enemies to Islam were an opening, not a repudiation.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عيينة فقال : اسن الله سلام وأمان ، فلا يكتب في النبذ والمحاربة

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna distinguishes repudiation from invitation: greeting recipients with peace applies to those who follow guidance, including those who accept Islam or jizya; repudiation brings disavowal and curse.
rows.anchor: فمن دعى إلى الله فأجاب ودعى إلى الجزية فأجاب فقد اتبع الهدى ، وأما النبذ فإنما هو البراءة واللعنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-basmala explanation can coexist with Uthman's report: the sura's status confused the Companions, its distinct name suggests a separate sura, and omitting the basmala suggests it may be part of another.
rows.anchor: لا يعارض هذا خبر ابن عباس عن عثمان رضي الله عنهما ، بل هو شبيه لما نزلت من غير بسملة للمعنى المذكور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet or Muslims recognized a sura's ending when the basmala was revealed; Abu Shama grades the report as hasan.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يعرف فصل السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the basmala normally marked a sura's end, its absence left the status uncertain; the Companions therefore left a small separation from al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: فلما اشتبه أمرها تركوا كتابة البسملة في أولها وفصلوها عن الأنفال قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two suras share treaty repudiation, the Sacred Mosque's guardianship by the pious, the impurity of polytheists, and the principle that believers' small numbers or opponents' large numbers do not decide victory.
rows.anchor: في كل منهمت من نبذ العهد إلى من خيف نقضه ، وأن المسجد الحرام لا يصلح لولايته إلا المتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shared themes also include repeated calls to jihad, promised provision, alms and booty, and spending; together they trace the Prophet's mission from its beginning through its middle to its end.
rows.anchor: والحث على الجهاد في غيبر موضع ، وضمان الغنى كما أشار إليه في الأنفال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the connection is so clear that the suras' close fit itself warrants placing them together without a basmala between them.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير في كتابه : اتصالها بالأنفال أوضح من أن يتكلف بتوجيهه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains that al-Anfal covers fighting, flight, captives, and believers' alliances, while Bara'a covers treaty repudiation, asylum, and related rules; both treat one subject.
rows.anchor: فالتحمت السورتان أعظم التحام ، ثم عاد الكلام إلى حكم المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfal says to renounce a treaty openly when treachery is feared but to honor it when safe; Bara'a begins by naming those whose treaty is renounced, clarifying the earlier rule.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فلما ذكر في آخر التي قبلها أمر العهد تارة بنبذه إلى من خيفت خيانته كائنا من كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning repentance for those near to deviation alongside the steadfast, the passage turns to those who did deviate without naming their fault, preserving their dignity and consoling them.
rows.anchor: ولما صرح بالتوبة على من قارب الزيغ وخلط معهم أهل الثبات إشارة إلى أن كل أحد فقير إلى الغني الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening phrase means that God had indeed turned toward and forgiven the three who had been left behind.
rows.anchor: وعلى } أي ولقد تاب الله على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were left behind through the Messenger's boycott, as he and the people stopped speaking to them while their judgment awaited God's decision.
rows.anchor: خلفوا } أي خلفهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالهجران ونهى الناس عن كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's being constricted despite its spaciousness uses an elevated expression to stress the severity: everywhere felt narrow to them.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى عظيم الأمر بأداة الاستعلاء فقال : { عليهم الأرض } اي كلها { بما رحبت } اي مع شدة اتساعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure was severe because they disobeyed the Messenger, withheld companionship, preferred themselves, and committed other grave offenses.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما عملوه من التخلف عن أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عظيما بمجرد المخالفة ثم يترك المواساة ثم بالرغبة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says fear of God's majesty can be grounded on the conviction that no cause leads to Him except through Him, since He encompasses all things.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه يكفي في الخوف من جلاله للانقطاع إليه مجرد الظن بأنه لا سبب إليه إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests ثم marks the length of their ordeal and fear, and God's favor in eventually returning them.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون التعبير - { ثم } إشارة إلى عظيم ما قاسوا من الأهوال وما تراقبوا إليه من مراتب الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay in judgment singled them out because of their high prior standing as leaders; even a slight lapse by guides is weighty.
rows.anchor: إنما خصوا عن رفائقهم بأن أرجئوا لأمر الله لعلو مقامهم بما لهم من السابقة ورسوخ القدم في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the grave disobedience of leaving the Messenger and failing to support him, God's second repentance purified them and raised them toward greater knowledge and closeness.
rows.anchor: { ثم تاب عليهم } أي رجع بهم بعد التوبة إلى مقام من مقامات سلامة الفطرة الذي هو أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first repentance enables them to return to their original sound disposition, steadfastness, religious excellence, and the character of the earliest believers.
rows.anchor: توبة { ليتوبوا } أي ليرجعوا إلى ما تقتضيه الفطرة الأولى من الثبات على ما كانوا عليه من الإحسان في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests ثم may signal the length of their ordeal and God's favor; their high prior rank explains the delayed ruling, since a small lapse by leaders is more serious than much by others.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون التعبير - { ثم } إشارة إلى عظيم ما قاسوا من الأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawwab emphasizes that God accepts repentance even after grave and repeated sins; al-Rahim emphasizes His preserving and abundantly favoring the servants He wills.
rows.anchor: { التواب } أي البليغ التوبة على من تاب وإن عظم جرمه وتكررت توبته ذنوبه { الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to fear God and be with the truthful applies to every believer: it makes the deficient catch up and urges those already ahead to preserve their lead.
rows.anchor: ولعله اخرج الأمر مخرج العموم ليشمل كل مؤمن , فمن كان مقصرا كانت آمره له باللحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase be with the truthful includes even the lowest degree of companionship, being physically present with them.
rows.anchor: ولعله عبر ب { مع } ليشمل أدنى الدرجات , وهو الكون بالجثت

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Al-Biqai notes that al-Bukhari records Ka'b's account of the repentance of one of the three in several places in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: وقد روى ابخاري توبة كعب أحد هؤلاء الثلاثة رضي الله عنهم في مواضع من صحيصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against people who imagine worldly life continues forever, the verse confines its likeness to fleeting vegetation, affirming resurrection and warning against oppression and unjust pride.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ينكرونه ويعتقدون بقاء الدنيا وأنها إنما هي أرحام تدفع وأرض تبلغ دائما بلا انقضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening إنما is a restrictive contrast: worldly enjoyment ends quickly after reaching its peak.
rows.anchor: { إنما } فهو قصر قلب { مثل الحياة الدنيا } التي تتنافسون فيها في سرعة انقضائها وانقراض نعيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from heaven makes vegetation flourish throughout the earth, including grain, fruits, and herbs eaten by people and livestock; the imagery also points to resurrection.
rows.anchor: فشبهه بأمر النبات وانه قليل يبلغ منتهاه فتصبح الأرض منه بلاقع بعد ذلك الاخضرار والينوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth takes on visible and hidden beauty from its plants; its owners strongly imagine they can harvest its produce, unaware of what comes next.
rows.anchor: أخذت الأرض } أي التي لها أهلية النبات { زخرفها وازينت } بأنواع ذلك النبات زينة منها الجلي ومنها الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command, such as extreme cold or heat by night or day, can turn the flourishing crop into harvested remnants, as if it had never been beautiful or abundant.
rows.anchor: { أتاها أمرنا } اي الذي لا يرد من البرد أو الحر المفرطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vanished crop illustrates the world's rapid loss of prosperity; God details signs like this for people who think, and the author defines parable, intermixture, and adornment.
rows.anchor: فكان حال الدنيا في سرعة انقضائها وانقراض نعيمها بعد عظيم إقباله كحال نبات الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the expression turning one's eyes away from people, عن means moving past them toward others.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { ولاتعد عيناك عنهم } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about combining their wealth with yours glosses إلى as joining or mixing possessions.
rows.anchor: { ولا تأكلون أموالهم } - ضاميها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in the phrase about approaching wives means being physically joined to them.
rows.anchor: { الرفث - مفضين - إلى نسائكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on resolving to marry is explained as intending to make the marriage contract.
rows.anchor: { ولا تعزموا } ) 77 [ البقرة : 235 ] اي على النكاح وأنتم تنوون عقدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the highest assembly means listening attentively; سمع الله لمن حمده means God responds to the one who praises Him.
rows.anchor: { إلى الملا الأعلى } ) 77 [ الصافات : 8 ] سمع الله - أي مستجيبا - لمن حمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the corrupter by distinguishing him from the reformer.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { والله يعلم المفسد } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allusion to those who swear off their wives glosses their oath as abstaining from marital intercourse.
rows.anchor: { والذين يؤلون } - ممتعين { من } وطء 77 ( { نسائهم } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those covered by blindness cannot benefit from signs: guidance along a physical road requires sight, while guidance along the spiritual road requires insight.
rows.anchor: فكان كالأعمى الذي زاد على عدم بصره عدم العقل فلا بصرولا بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes sight-seeking with the eyes from the heart's search for knowledge, and defines blindness and perception for both eye and heart.
rows.anchor: والنظر : طلب الرؤية بتقليب البصر , ونظر القلب طلب العلم بالفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete sovereignty and favor mean He owes no one anything; the author then frames the point as God not wronging people, who wrong themselves by choice under His creation.
rows.anchor: { إن الله } وأحسن منه ان يقال : ولما كان التقدير : إذا علمت ذلك فخفف عنك بعض ما أنت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who deny resurrection live as though time were ample and danger remote, but on gathering their worldly stay seems only a small daytime hour.
rows.anchor: يرون يوم الحشر من الأهوال ما يستقصرون معه مدة لبثهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their brief stay gains them only mutual recognition, increasing regret because they cannot support or help one another as they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: إلا ساعة } أي حقيرة { من النهار } وقوله : { يتعارفون بينهم } حال ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who denied meeting God truly lost by taking transient lowly goods over enduring noble reward; the explicit label generalizes the judgment, and their failure to be guided was habitual.
rows.anchor: { قد خسر } أي حقا { الذين كذبوا } اظهر موضع الإضمار تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف مستهنين { بلقاء الله } أي الملك الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Muhammad sees some promised punishment before death, it will comfort him; otherwise, after his death the return to God brings a still greater vindication.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { قد خسر } : { وإما نرينك } أي إراءة عظيمة قبل وفاتك { بعض الذي نعدهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by mentioning seeing punishment first to imply it after death, and mentioning death second to imply it before death.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر أولا الإراءة دليلا على حذفها ثانيا , والوفاة ثانيا دليلا على حذفها أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم can mark the interval from death to resurrection; شهيد points by metonymy to the punishment that follows God's witnessing of their deeds.
rows.anchor: يمكنأن يكون على بابها , فتكون مشيرة إلى التراخي بين ابتداء رجوعهم بالموت وآخره إلى بالقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every former nation had a messenger who came with proofs in worldly life and will report their response at the final gathering; God judges all justly, assigning immediate or delayed punishment without wrong.
rows.anchor: { ولكل أمة } أي من الأمم التي خلت قبلك { رسول } يدعوهم إلى الله

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani explains that reported speech may quote actual words or convey speech without reproducing its exact wording; promise may mean either reward or punishment here.
rows.anchor: والقول كلام مضمن في ذكره بالحكاية وقد يكون كلام لا يعبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad has no independent control of harm or benefit, even for himself; all capacity is subject to God's will, and every community has an appointed term that cannot be advanced or delayed.
rows.anchor: { لا أملك لنفسي } فضلا عن غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the context concerns vengeance, harm comes first; blessings are more numerous, so people should be grateful rather than wish for harm, and the author explains the forms of the words for delay and advance.
rows.anchor: قدم الضر منبها على أن نعمه أكثر من نقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At drowning, Pharaoh professes belief in God and in the Israelites' faith, then claims to be among the Muslims; his repeated confession stresses panic and attempted sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال آمنت } أي أوقعت إيمان الداعي لي من التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read innahu with a kasra and treat the clause as replacing I have believed; the majority reading can be understood with an implied bi, acknowledging that there is no deity except God.
rows.anchor: في قراءة حمزة والكسائي بالكسر مؤكدا من شدة الجزع : { أنه } وعلى تقدير الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His explicit reference to the faith of the Children of Israel removes any ambiguity about the belief he professes.
rows.anchor: أراد الإعلام بغاية صدقه فقال : { آمنت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying I am among the Muslims repeats the acceptance Pharaoh once rejected proudly; his claim to deep submission comes too late because faith must concern the unseen.
rows.anchor: فكرر قبول ما كان دعي إليه فأباه استكبارا , وعبر بما دل على ادعاء الرسوخ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Now? rebukes a reply made when faith in the unseen can no longer benefit him; Pharaoh had disobeyed throughout the prior call and was deeply corrupt.
rows.anchor: بقوله على لسان الحال أو جبريل عليه السلام أو ملك الموت أو غيره من الجنود عليهم السلام : { آلئن } أي أتجيب إلى ما دعيت إليه في هذا الحين الذي لا ينفع فيه الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke may be spoken by God, Gabriel, the Angel of Death, or another of the angelic hosts.
rows.anchor: بقوله على لسان الحال أو جبريل عليه السلام أو ملك الموت أو غيره من الجنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves Pharaoh's soulless but intact body as a clear sign for later people that even the strongest ruler is a weak servant who is punished for disobedience.
rows.anchor: فاليوم ننجيك } أي تنجية عظيمة . ولما كان ذلك سارا وكانت المساءة بما يفهم السرور إنكاء , قال دالا على أن ذلك يعد نزع روحه : { ببدنك } أي من غير روح وهو كامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects claims that Pharaoh's profession here proves his faith: the consensus of religious communities calls him among the most unbelieving, and the claim would trivialize sin.
rows.anchor: وقد ادعى بعض الملحدين إيمانه بهذه الآية إرادة لما يعيذ الله منه من حل العقد الواجب من أن فرعون من أكفر الكفرة بإجماه أهل الملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pattern in earlier nations was to punish those who rejected messengers and then save believers, just as He will save Muhammad and his followers.
rows.anchor: ثم ننجي الرسل ومن آمن بهم حقا علينا ذلك للعدل بين العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense rescue re-enacts past events as a warning; ثم signals the prolonged trial and elevated rank of rescue, while omission of the opposite clause keeps focus on glad tidings.
rows.anchor: وجاء به مضارعا خكايى للأحوال الماضية وتصويرا لها تحذيرا لهم من مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved include everyone who truly believed with the messengers, even those at the lowest rank, encouraging others to emulate them.
rows.anchor: { والذبن آمنوا } اي بالرسل وهم معهم في زمانهم ولو كانوا في أدنى درجات الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's obligation to save believers applies in every age, even without a living messenger among them; alternatively, the author parses كذلك as a subject and ننج المؤمنين as its predicate.
rows.anchor: لا , بل { كذلك } أي الحقوق { حقا علينا } على ما لنا من العظمة { ننج المؤمنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next answer shows Muhammad's firmness: if people doubt his religion, he does not doubt its truth and invites them to examine their own worship.
rows.anchor: ناشبة كل المناسبة أن أتبعت الأمر بجواب آخر دال على ثباته صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's miraculous arrangement, wisdom, laws, rare insights, and knowledge suffice as proof; each verse exposes the weakness of their accusation that the Messenger invented it.
rows.anchor: وكان فيما يشهد به إعجاز القرآن ببديع نظمه وباهر حكمه وحكمه وزاجر غرائبه ووافر علمه ما يغني عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers the repeated accusation of invention by challenging the Arabs, his peers in language and native context, to produce ten fabricated suras like it.
rows.anchor: { قل } أي لهم على سبيل التنزل { فأتوا } يا معاشر العرب فإنكم مثلي في العربية واللسان والمولد والزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten means complete units, each with a whole meaning; they must match the Qur'an's length, eloquence, sweetness, strength, and grace, though fabrication frees them from truthful meanings and sound foundations.
rows.anchor: { بعشر سور } اي قطع , كل قطعة منها تحيط بمعنى تام يستدل فيها عليه { مثله } أي تكون العشر مثل جميع القرآن في طوله

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi cites al-Mubarrad for the reading that the challengers need only match eloquence, not the Qur'an's true meanings or sound construction.
rows.anchor: ذكره البغوي عن المبرد , وقد مضى في البقرة عند

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says a challenger first asks for several examples of what the opponent claims to do, then, after showing failure, asks for just one.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وشأن من يريد تعجيز شخص أن يطالبه أولا بأن يفعل أمثالا مما يفعل هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staged demand addresses those who insist the Qur'an is fabricated while claiming it lacks wisdom and guidance.
rows.anchor: وادعيتم مكابرة أنه مفترى فارغ عن الحكم فأتوا بعشر مثله في مجرد البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge progresses from the whole Qur'an, to an enduring inability shared by humans and jinn, to one sura in Yunus, then ten fabricated suras here, easing one constraint while retaining another.
rows.anchor: [ الطور : 34 ] أي في التحتم والتطبيق على الوقائع وما يحدث ويتجدد شيئا في إثر شيء ثم قطع بعد عجزهم بدوام عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier challenges varied: Yunus asked for one sura without detailed divisions; Hud allows fabricated meaning but asks for ten; Baqara later again asks for one sura and states permanent inability.
rows.anchor: ثم تحدوا في سورة يونس عليه السلام بسورة واحدة مثل جميع القرآن غير معتنين فيها بالتفصيل إلى السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each sura sets a different challenge; the author says fuller understanding comes from the passages in Yunus, Baqara, Isra, and Tur.
rows.anchor: تحديهم بسورة , أي قطعة واحدة مقرونا ذلك بالإخبار بدوام عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eloquence has three levels; only its highest level is miraculous, and the challenge targets that level rather than commanding anyone to fabricate revelation.
rows.anchor: والبلاغة ثلاث طبقات فأعلاها معجز , وأوسطها وأدناها ممكن , والتحدي وقع بالعليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation to summon whomever they can means anyone they can induce to obey them, and all those ranks remain beneath God, whom Arabs acknowledge as supreme.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وادعوا من استطعتم } أي طلبتم أن يطيعكم ففعل , ولما كانت الرتب كلها تحت رتبته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure also proves by a fortiori reasoning that no helper below them in eloquence can succeed either.
rows.anchor: فإن كل ظهير من سواهم دونهم في البلاغة , فعجزهم عجز لغيرهم بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no one answers the challenge, all people should know the Qur'an was revealed with God's knowledge; an ordinary human could not access or invent divine speech against the established order.
rows.anchor: إلا ملتبسا { بعلم الله } أي المحيط بكل شيء قدرة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the unexpressed subject of answering may be those summoned, with لكم referring to the polytheists; if another god existed, it could produce speech matching God's, and their idols cannot save them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ضمير { يستجيبوا } ل ( من ) { استطعتم } و { لكم } للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof leads to the urgent invitation to submit fully to Islam, with a warning against delay.
rows.anchor: { فهل أنتم مسلمون * } أي منقادون أتم انقياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose deeds seek worldly life and adornment receive their full worldly recompense, such as status and wealth, without reduction; their bodies, souls, and religions are still impoverished in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أي الدنيا بالجاه والمال ونحو ذلك { وهم فيها } أي في الأعمال أو الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This worldly recompense explains why punishment is withheld during their period of respite despite their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وفي الجملتين بيان سبب حبس العذاب عنهم في مدة إمهالهم مع سوء أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those people receive only Fire in the afterlife after taking their full reward in this world; their works collapse because they lack a sound foundation and are empty forms.
rows.anchor: { أولئك } أي البعداء البغضاء { الذين ليس لهم } أي شيء من الأشياء { في الآخرة إلا النار } أي لسوء أعمالهم واستيفائهم جزاءها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines adornment as beautification by clothing, jewelry, or appearance; full recompense as delivering a right completely; and the nullification of work through the image of a spoiled stomach.
rows.anchor: والزينة : تحسين الشيء بغيره من لبسه أو حلية أو هيئة ؛ والتوفية : تأدية الحق على تمام ؛ وحبوط العمل : بطلانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person on clear proof from his Lord seeks the afterlife and bases deeds on a firm foundation; the following witness is the Qur'an, or alternatively the proof is supported by an Arab Messenger's miraculous speech.
rows.anchor: فهو يريد الآخرة ويبني أفعاله على أساس ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah of Moses preceded the Qur'anic witness and also serves as an authoritative guide and mercy for those who follow it.
rows.anchor: حال كونه { إماما } يحق الاقتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Jews told the polytheists that they were more rightly guided than the Muslims, illustrating the objection to equating the guided with the rebellious.
rows.anchor: كمن قال من اليهود للمشركين : أنتم أهدى منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Rummani transmits from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak that Noah's son was Canaan, Noah's biological son.
rows.anchor: أي كنعان وهو لصلبه - نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son was separate from his father in location and religion because he was an unbeliever; Noah tenderly calls him my son and urges him to board with the believers.
rows.anchor: أي عن أبيه في مكانه وفي دينه لأنه كان كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's urgent plea shows prophetic compassion cannot soften hearts without God's permission, even amid terrifying signs; his son is so harsh he does not call Noah father.
rows.anchor: ليست سبا للين القلوب وخضوع النفوس ما لم يأذن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son says he will seek refuge on a mountain from the flood, but Noah answers that no mountain or other thing can protect anyone from God's decree except God's mercy, manifested through the ark or the one God has mercy upon.
rows.anchor: { لا عاصم } أي لا مانع نم جبل ولا غير موجود { اليوم } أي لأحد { من أمر الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the waters rise and overwhelm everything, Noah's son disobeys his father as he disobeyed God, goes to the mountain, cannot rejoin the ark, and drowns.
rows.anchor: فعلا وطما وغلب وعتا فهال الأمر وزاد على الحد والقدر
